speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
कर्मायत्तं फलं पुंसां बुद्धिः कर्मानुसारिणी।
तथाऽपि सुधिया भाव्यं सुविचार्यैव कुर्वता ॥
iast:
karmāyattaṃ phalaṃ puṃsāṃ buddhiḥ karmānusāriṇī|
tathā'pi sudhiyā bhāvyaṃ suvicāryaiva kurvatā ||
english: The fruits people reap depend on their actions, and the mind follows their actions. Even so, the wise should act only after careful thought.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
खल्वाटो दिवसेश्वरस्य किरणैः संतापितो मस्तके वाञ्छन्देशमनातपं विधिवशात्तालस्य मूलं गतः।
तत्राऽप्यस्य महाफलेन पतता भग्नं सशब्दं शिरः प्रायो गच्छति यत्र भाग्यरहितस्तत्रैव यान्त्यापदः ॥
iast:
khalvāṭo divaseśvarasya kiraṇaiḥ saṃtāpito mastake vāñchandeśamanātapaṃ vidhivaśāttālasya mūlaṃ gataḥ|
tatrā'pyasya mahāphalena patatā bhagnaṃ saśabdaṃ śiraḥ prāyo gacchati yatra bhāgyarahitastatraiva yāntyāpadaḥ ||
english: A bald man, his head scorched by the rays of the sun, seeking a shady spot, went by fate to the foot of a palm tree; there too, a great falling fruit broke his head with a crack. Usually, wherever the luckless go, misfortunes go too.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
गजभुजङ्गमयोरपि बन्धनं शशिदिवाकरयोर्ग्रहपीडनम्।
मतिमताञ्च विलोक्य दरिद्रतां विधिरहो ! बलवानिति मे मतिः ॥
iast:
gajabhujaṅgamayorapi bandhanaṃ śaśidivākarayorgrahapīḍanam|
matimatāñca vilokya daridratāṃ vidhiraho ! balavāniti me matiḥ ||
english: Seeing even elephants and snakes in bonds, the moon and sun troubled by eclipse, and the intelligent in poverty, my view is: ah, fate is strong.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
सृजति तावदशेषगुणाकरं पुरुषरत्नमलङ्करणं भुवः।
तदपि तत्क्षणभङ्गि करोति चे- दहह ! कष्टमपण्डितता विधेः ॥
iast:
sṛjati tāvadaśeṣaguṇākaraṃ puruṣaratnamalaṅkaraṇaṃ bhuvaḥ|
tadapi tatkṣaṇabhaṅgi karoti ce- dahaha ! kaṣṭamapaṇḍitatā vidheḥ ||
english: Fate creates a jewel of a person, a mine of every virtue, an ornament to the earth, and then makes him perish in a moment. Alas, what a pity, the folly of fate!

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
पत्रं नैव यदा करीरविटपे दोषो वसन्तस्य किं-नोलूकोऽप्यवलोकते यदि दिवा सूर्यस्य किं दूषणम्।
धारा नैव पतन्ति चातकमुखे मेघस्य किं दूषणं यत्पूर्वं विधिना ललाटलिखितं तन्मार्जितुं कः क्षमः ॥
iast:
patraṃ naiva yadā karīraviṭape doṣo vasantasya kiṃ-nolūko'pyavalokate yadi divā sūryasya kiṃ dūṣaṇam|
dhārā naiva patanti cātakamukhe meghasya kiṃ dūṣaṇaṃ yatpūrvaṃ vidhinā lalāṭalikhitaṃ tanmārjituṃ kaḥ kṣamaḥ ||
english: If the karira bush has no leaves, is spring at fault? If the owl does not see by day, is it the sun's fault? If rain does not fall into the chataka's mouth, is it the cloud's fault? Who can wipe away what the Creator wrote on the forehead long ago?

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
नमस्यामो देवान्ननु हतविधेस्तेऽपि वशगा विधिर्वन्द्यः सोऽपि प्रतिनियतकर्मैकफलदः।
फलं कर्मायत्तं किममरगणैः किञ्च विधिना नमस्तत्कर्मभ्यो विधिरपि न येभ्यः प्रभवति ॥
iast:
namasyāmo devānnanu hatavidheste'pi vaśagā vidhirvandyaḥ so'pi pratiniyatakarmaikaphaladaḥ|
phalaṃ karmāyattaṃ kimamaragaṇaiḥ kiñca vidhinā namastatkarmabhyo vidhirapi na yebhyaḥ prabhavati ||
english: We bow to the gods; but they are under the power of wretched fate. Fate is to be revered; but it gives only the fixed fruit of actions. If the fruit depends on action, what use are the gods, and what use is fate? Salutations to those actions, over which even fate has no power.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
अपि च - ब्रह्मा येन कुलालवन्नियमितो ब्रह्माण्डभाण्डोदरे विष्णुर्येन दशावतारगहने क्षिप्तो महासंकटे।
रुद्रो येन कपालपाणिपुटके भिक्षाटनं कारितः सूर्यो भ्राम्यति नित्यमेव गगने तस्मै नमः कर्मणे ॥
iast:
api ca - brahmā yena kulālavanniyamito brahmāṇḍabhāṇḍodare viṣṇuryena daśāvatāragahane kṣipto mahāsaṃkaṭe|
rudro yena kapālapāṇipuṭake bhikṣāṭanaṃ kāritaḥ sūryo bhrāmyati nityameva gagane tasmai namaḥ karmaṇe ||
english: Moreover: by which Brahma is held like a potter within the pot of the universe, Vishnu is thrown into the great trouble of ten incarnations, Rudra is made to beg with a skull in his hand, and the sun wanders the sky every day: salutations to that karma.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
नैवाकृतिः फलति नैव कुलं न शीलं विद्यापि नैव न च यत्नकृताऽपि सेवा।
भाग्यानि पूर्वतपसा खलु सञ्चितानि काले फलन्ति पुरुषस्य यथैव वृक्षाः ॥
iast:
naivākṛtiḥ phalati naiva kulaṃ na śīlaṃ vidyāpi naiva na ca yatnakṛtā'pi sevā|
bhāgyāni pūrvatapasā khalu sañcitāni kāle phalanti puruṣasya yathaiva vṛkṣāḥ ||
english: Neither appearance bears fruit, nor family, nor character, nor even learning, nor service done with effort. Only the fortunes stored up by past austerities bear fruit for a person in time, as trees do.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
वने रणे शत्रुजलाग्निमध्ये महार्णवे पर्वतमस्तके वा।
सुप्तं प्रमत्तं विषमस्थितं वा रक्षन्ति पुण्यानि पुरा कृतानि ॥
iast:
vane raṇe śatrujalāgnimadhye mahārṇave parvatamastake vā|
suptaṃ pramattaṃ viṣamasthitaṃ vā rakṣanti puṇyāni purā kṛtāni ||
english: In the forest, in battle, amid enemies, water and fire, on the great ocean or a mountain top, whether asleep, careless or in danger, the good deeds done before protect a person.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
या साधूंश्च खलान्करोति विदुषो मूर्खान्हितान्द्वेषिणः प्रत्यक्षं कुरुते परोक्षममृतं हालाहलं तत्क्षणात्।
तामाराधय सत्क्रियां भगवतीं भोक्तुं फलं वाञ्छितं हे साधो ! व्यसनैर्गुणेषु विपुलेष्वास्थां वृथा माकृथाः ॥
iast:
yā sādhūṃśca khalānkaroti viduṣo mūrkhānhitāndveṣiṇaḥ pratyakṣaṃ kurute parokṣamamṛtaṃ hālāhalaṃ tatkṣaṇāt|
tāmārādhaya satkriyāṃ bhagavatīṃ bhoktuṃ phalaṃ vāñchitaṃ he sādho ! vyasanairguṇeṣu vipuleṣvāsthāṃ vṛthā mākṛthāḥ ||
english: Right action can make the wicked good, fools wise, enemies friends, the hidden plain, and poison nectar in a moment. Good person, worship that goddess, right action, to gain the fruit you desire; do not vainly put your trust in many virtues won with toil.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
गुणवदगुणवद्वा कुर्वता कार्यमादौ परिणतिरवधार्या यत्नतः पण्डितेन।
अतिरभसकृतानां कर्मणामाविपत्ते-र्भवति हृदयदाही शल्यतुल्यो विपाकः ॥
iast:
guṇavadaguṇavadvā kurvatā kāryamādau pariṇatiravadhāryā yatnataḥ paṇḍitena|
atirabhasakṛtānāṃ karmaṇāmāvipatte-rbhavati hṛdayadāhī śalyatulyo vipākaḥ ||
english: Whether doing something good or bad, the wise should first carefully consider how it will turn out. The result of acts done in great haste burns the heart like a thorn until death.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
स्थाल्यां वैदूर्यमय्यां पचति तिलकणांश्चन्दनैरिन्धनाद्यैः सौवर्णैर्लाङ्गलाग्रैर्विलिखति वसुधामर्कमूलस्य हेतोः।
कृत्वा कर्पूरखण्डान्वृतिमिह कुरुते कोद्रवाणां समन्ता- त्प्राप्येमां कर्मभूमिं न चरति मनुजो यस्तपो मन्दभाग्यः ॥
iast:
sthālyāṃ vaidūryamayyāṃ pacati tilakaṇāṃścandanairindhanādyaiḥ sauvarṇairlāṅgalāgrairvilikhati vasudhāmarkamūlasya hetoḥ|
kṛtvā karpūrakhaṇḍānvṛtimiha kurute kodravāṇāṃ samantā- tprāpyemāṃ karmabhūmiṃ na carati manujo yastapo mandabhāgyaḥ ||
english: He cooks sesame seeds in a pot of beryl with sandalwood for fuel; he ploughs the earth with golden ploughshares for the sake of arka roots; he builds a fence of camphor around a field of kodo millet: such is the unlucky person who, having reached this land of action, does not practise austerity.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
मज्जत्वम्भसि यातु मेरुशिखरं शत्रूञ्जयत्वाहवे वाणिज्यं कृषिसेवनादिसकला विद्याः कलाः शिक्षताम्।
आकाशं विपुलं प्रयातु खगवत्कृत्वा प्रयत्नं महा- न्नाभाव्यं भवतीह कर्मवशतो भाव्यस्य नाशः कुतः ॥
iast:
majjatvambhasi yātu meruśikharaṃ śatrūñjayatvāhave vāṇijyaṃ kṛṣisevanādisakalā vidyāḥ kalāḥ śikṣatām|
ākāśaṃ vipulaṃ prayātu khagavatkṛtvā prayatnaṃ mahā- nnābhāvyaṃ bhavatīha karmavaśato bhāvyasya nāśaḥ kutaḥ ||
english: Let him dive into the water, go to the top of Meru, conquer enemies in battle, learn trade, farming, service and all the arts and sciences, fly through the wide sky like a bird with great effort: what is not to be will not happen here, through the power of karma, and how can what is to be be destroyed?

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
भीमं वनं भवति तस्य पुरं प्रधानं सर्वे जनाः सुजनतामुपयान्ति तस्य।
कृत्स्ना च भूर्भवति सन्निधिरत्नपूर्णा यस्यास्ति पूर्वसुकृतं विपुलं नरस्य ॥
iast:
bhīmaṃ vanaṃ bhavati tasya puraṃ pradhānaṃ sarve janāḥ sujanatāmupayānti tasya|
kṛtsnā ca bhūrbhavati sannidhiratnapūrṇā yasyāsti pūrvasukṛtaṃ vipulaṃ narasya ||
english: For the person who has abundant past good deeds, a fearsome forest becomes a chief city, all people become good to him, and the whole earth becomes full of treasures and jewels.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
को लाभो गुणिसङ्गमः किमसुखं प्राज्ञेतरैः सङ्गतिः का हानिः समयच्युतिर्निपुणता का धर्मतत्त्वे रतिः।
कः शूरो विजितेन्द्रियः प्रियतमा काऽनुव्रता किं धनं विद्या किं सुखमप्रवासगमनं राज्यं किमाज्ञाफलम् ॥
iast:
ko lābho guṇisaṅgamaḥ kimasukhaṃ prājñetaraiḥ saṅgatiḥ kā hāniḥ samayacyutirnipuṇatā kā dharmatattve ratiḥ|
kaḥ śūro vijitendriyaḥ priyatamā kā'nuvratā kiṃ dhanaṃ vidyā kiṃ sukhamapravāsagamanaṃ rājyaṃ kimājñāphalam ||
english: What is gain? The company of the virtuous. What is unhappiness? Company with fools. What is loss? Missing the right moment. What is skill? Delight in the truth of dharma. Who is a hero? One who has mastered the senses. Who is dearest? A faithful partner. What is wealth? Learning. What is happiness? Not having to live away from home. What is a kingdom? Having one's word obeyed.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
मालतीकुसुमस्येव द्वे गतीह मनस्विनः।
मूर्ध्नि सर्वस्य लोकस्य शीर्यते वन एव वा ॥
iast:
mālatīkusumasyeva dve gatīha manasvinaḥ|
mūrdhni sarvasya lokasya śīryate vana eva vā ||
english: Like a jasmine flower, a high-minded person has two courses here: on the head of the whole world, or withering in the forest.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
अप्रियवचनदरिद्रैः प्रियवचनाढ्यैः स्वदारपरितुष्टैः।
परपरिवादनिवृत्तैः क्वचित्क्वचिन्मण्डिता वसुधा ॥
iast:
apriyavacanadaridraiḥ priyavacanāḍhyaiḥ svadāraparituṣṭaiḥ|
paraparivādanivṛttaiḥ kvacitkvacinmaṇḍitā vasudhā ||
english: Poor in harsh words, rich in kind words, content with their own spouses, and turned away from slandering others: only here and there is the earth adorned by such people.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
कदर्थितस्यापि हि धैर्यवृत्तेर्न शक्यते धैर्यगुणाः प्रमार्ष्टुम्।
अधोमुखस्यापि कृतस्य वह्नेर्नाधः शिखा याति कदाचिदेव ॥
iast:
kadarthitasyāpi hi dhairyavṛtterna śakyate dhairyaguṇāḥ pramārṣṭum|
adhomukhasyāpi kṛtasya vahnernādhaḥ śikhā yāti kadācideva ||
english: Even when a steadfast person is ill-treated, the qualities of steadfastness cannot be wiped away; even when a fire is turned upside down, its flame never goes downward.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
कान्ताकटाक्षविशखा न लुनन्ति यस्य चित्तं न निर्दहति कोपकृशानुतापः।
कर्षन्ति भूरिविषयाश्च न लोभपाशै- र्लोकत्रयं जयति कृत्स्नमिदं स धीरः ॥
iast:
kāntākaṭākṣaviśakhā na lunanti yasya cittaṃ na nirdahati kopakṛśānutāpaḥ|
karṣanti bhūriviṣayāśca na lobhapāśai- rlokatrayaṃ jayati kṛtsnamidaṃ sa dhīraḥ ||
english: Whose mind is not pierced by the arrows of a lover's glances, not burnt by the fire of anger, and not dragged by the many objects of the senses with the nooses of greed: that steadfast person conquers all three worlds.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
एकेनापि हि शूरेण पादाक्रान्तं महीतलम्।
क्रियते भास्करेणेव स्फारस्फुरिततेजसा ॥
iast:
ekenāpi hi śūreṇa pādākrāntaṃ mahītalam|
kriyate bhāskareṇeva sphārasphuritatejasā ||
english: Even by one brave person the whole earth is brought under foot, as by the sun with its blazing brilliance.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
वह्निस्तस्य जलायते जलनिधिः कुल्यायते तत्क्षणा-न्मेरुः स्वल्पशिलायते मृगपतिः सद्यः कुरङ्गायते।
व्यालो माल्यगुणायते विषरसः पीयूषवर्षायते यस्याङ्गेऽखिललोकवल्लभतमं शीलं समुन्मीलति ॥
iast:
vahnistasya jalāyate jalanidhiḥ kulyāyate tatkṣaṇā-nmeruḥ svalpaśilāyate mṛgapatiḥ sadyaḥ kuraṅgāyate|
vyālo mālyaguṇāyate viṣarasaḥ pīyūṣavarṣāyate yasyāṅge'khilalokavallabhatamaṃ śīlaṃ samunmīlati ||
english: For one in whom good character, dearest of all to the whole world, blossoms, fire becomes like water, the ocean like a stream, Meru like a small stone, the lion like a deer, the snake like a garland of flowers, and poison like a shower of nectar, at once.

speaker: Bhartrihari
devanagari:
लज्जागुणौघजननीं जननीमिव स्वा-मत्यन्तशुद्धहृदयामनुवर्त्तमानाम्।
तेजस्विनः सुखमसूनपि संत्यजन्ति सत्यव्रतव्यसनिनो न पुनः प्रतिज्ञाम् ॥
iast:
lajjāguṇaughajananīṃ jananīmiva svā-matyantaśuddhahṛdayāmanuvarttamānām|
tejasvinaḥ sukhamasūnapi saṃtyajanti satyavratavyasanino na punaḥ pratijñām ||
english: Those of spirit, devoted to the vow of truth, will gladly give up even their life, but never their promise, which, like their own mother, is pure of heart, gives birth to a flood of virtues such as modesty, and always follows them.

speaker: Vaishampayana
devanagari:
द्वाःस्थं प्राह महाप्राज्ञो धृतराष्ट्रो महीपतिः ।
विदुरं द्रष्टुमिच्छामि तमिहानय माचिरम् ॥
iast:
dvāḥsthaṃ prāha mahāprājño dhṛtarāṣṭro mahīpatiḥ |
viduraṃ draṣṭumicchāmi tamihānaya māciram ||
english: Dhritarashtra, the very wise king, said to the doorkeeper: 'I wish to see Vidura. Bring him here without delay.'

speaker: Vaishampayana
devanagari:
प्रहितो धृतराष्ट्रेण दूतः क्षत्तारमब्रवीत् ।
ईश्वरस्त्वां महाराजो महाप्राज्ञ दिदृक्षति ॥
iast:
prahito dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa dūtaḥ kṣattāramabravīt |
īśvarastvāṃ mahārājo mahāprājña didṛkṣati ||
english: Sent by Dhritarashtra, the messenger said to the steward: 'The great king, your lord, wishes to see you, wise one.'

speaker: Vaishampayana
devanagari:
एवमुक्तस्तु विदुरः प्राप्य राजनिवेशनम् ।
अब्रवीद्धृतराष्ट्राय द्वाःस्थ मां प्रतिवेदय ॥
iast:
evamuktastu viduraḥ prāpya rājaniveśanam |
abravīddhṛtarāṣṭrāya dvāḥstha māṃ prativedaya ||
english: Told this, Vidura went to the king's dwelling and said: 'Doorkeeper, announce me to Dhritarashtra.'

speaker: doorkeeper
devanagari:
विदुरोऽयमनुप्राप्तो राजेन्द्र तव शासनात् ।
द्रष्टुमिच्छति ते पादौ किं करोतु प्रशाधि माम् ॥
iast:
viduro'yamanuprāpto rājendra tava śāsanāt |
draṣṭumicchati te pādau kiṃ karotu praśādhi mām ||
english: Vidura has come at your command, lord of kings. He wishes to see your feet. Tell me, what shall he do?

speaker: Dhritarashtra
devanagari:
प्रवेशय महाप्राज्ञं विदुरं दीर्घदर्शिनम् ।
अहं हि विदुरस्यास्य नाकाल्यो जातु दर्शने ॥
iast:
praveśaya mahāprājñaṃ viduraṃ dīrghadarśinam |
ahaṃ hi vidurasyāsya nākālyo jātu darśane ||
english: Bring in the wise, far-seeing Vidura. I am never unwilling to see this Vidura at any time.

speaker: doorkeeper
devanagari:
प्रविशान्तः पुरं क्षत्तर्महाराजस्य धीमतः ।
न हि ते दर्शनेऽकाल्यो जातु राजा ब्रवीति माम् ॥
iast:
praviśāntaḥ puraṃ kṣattarmahārājasya dhīmataḥ |
na hi te darśane'kālyo jātu rājā bravīti mām ||
english: Enter the inner palace of the wise great king, steward. The king tells me that seeing you is never untimely.

speaker: Vaishampayana
devanagari:
ततः प्रविश्य विदुरो धृतराष्ट्र निवेशनम् ।
अब्रवीत्प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं चिन्तयानं नराधिपम् ॥
iast:
tataḥ praviśya viduro dhṛtarāṣṭra niveśanam |
abravītprāñjalirvākyaṃ cintayānaṃ narādhipam ||
english: Then Vidura entered Dhritarashtra's chamber and, with folded hands, spoke to the king, who was lost in thought:

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
विदुरोऽहं महाप्राज्ञ सम्प्राप्तस्तव शासनात् ।
यदि किं चन कर्तव्यमयमस्मि प्रशाधि माम् ॥
iast:
viduro'haṃ mahāprājña samprāptastava śāsanāt |
yadi kiṃ cana kartavyamayamasmi praśādhi mām ||
english: I am Vidura, very wise one, come at your command. If there is anything to be done, here I am: command me.

speaker: Dhritarashtra
devanagari:
सञ्जयो विदुर प्राप्तो गर्हयित्वा च मां गतः ।
अजातशत्रोः श्वो वाक्यं सभामध्ये स वक्ष्यति ॥
iast:
sañjayo vidura prāpto garhayitvā ca māṃ gataḥ |
ajātaśatroḥ śvo vākyaṃ sabhāmadhye sa vakṣyati ||
english: Sanjaya came, Vidura, rebuked me and left. Tomorrow, in the middle of the assembly, he will speak Ajatashatru's message.

speaker: Dhritarashtra
devanagari:
तस्याद्य कुरुवीरस्य न विज्ञातं वचो मया ।
तन्मे दहति गात्राणि तदकार्षीत्प्रजागरम् ॥
iast:
tasyādya kuruvīrasya na vijñātaṃ vaco mayā |
tanme dahati gātrāṇi tadakārṣītprajāgaram ||
english: I have not learned today what that Kuru hero said. That burns my limbs; that has made me sleepless.

speaker: Dhritarashtra
devanagari:
जाग्रतो दह्यमानस्य श्रेयो यदिह पश्यसि ।
तद्ब्रूहि त्वं हि नस्तात धर्मार्थकुशलो ह्यसि ॥
iast:
jāgrato dahyamānasya śreyo yadiha paśyasi |
tadbrūhi tvaṃ hi nastāta dharmārthakuśalo hyasi ||
english: Tell me what you see as good for one who lies awake, burning like this; for you, dear one, are skilled in dharma and in worldly affairs.

speaker: Dhritarashtra
devanagari:
यतः प्राप्तः सञ्जयः पाण्डवेभ्यो
न मे यथावन्मनसः प्रशान्तिः ।
सवेन्द्रियाण्यप्रकृतिं गतानि
किं वक्ष्यतीत्येव हि मेऽद्य चिन्ता ॥
iast:
yataḥ prāptaḥ sañjayaḥ pāṇḍavebhyo
na me yathāvanmanasaḥ praśāntiḥ |
savendriyāṇyaprakṛtiṃ gatāni
kiṃ vakṣyatītyeva hi me'dya cintā ||
english: Since Sanjaya came back from the Pandavas, my mind has had no real peace. All my senses are out of order; my only thought today is, what will he say?

speaker: Dhritarashtra
devanagari:
तन्मे ब्रूहि विदुर त्वं यथावन्
मनीषितं सर्वमजातशत्रोः ।
यथा च नस्तात हितं भवेच्च
प्रजाश्च सर्वाः सुखिता भवेयुः ॥
iast:
tanme brūhi vidura tvaṃ yathāvan
manīṣitaṃ sarvamajātaśatroḥ |
yathā ca nastāta hitaṃ bhavecca
prajāśca sarvāḥ sukhitā bhaveyuḥ ||
english: So tell me truly, Vidura, everything Ajatashatru has in mind, and what would be good for us, dear one, so that all the people may be happy.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अभियुक्तं बलवता दुर्बलं हीनसाधनम् ।
हृतस्वं कामिनं चोरमाविशन्ति प्रजागराः ॥
iast:
abhiyuktaṃ balavatā durbalaṃ hīnasādhanam |
hṛtasvaṃ kāminaṃ coramāviśanti prajāgarāḥ ||
english: Sleeplessness takes hold of a weak person without resources who is attacked by a strong one, of one whose wealth has been taken, of one full of desire, and of a thief.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
कच्चिदेतैर्महादोषैर्न स्पृष्टोऽसि नराधिप ।
कच्चिन्न परवित्तेषु गृध्यन्विपरितप्यसे ॥
iast:
kaccidetairmahādoṣairna spṛṣṭo'si narādhipa |
kaccinna paravitteṣu gṛdhyanviparitapyase ||
english: I hope you are not touched by these great faults, lord of men. I hope you are not tormented by longing for others' wealth.

speaker: Dhritarashtra
devanagari:
श्रोतुमिच्छामि ते धर्म्यं परं नैःश्रेयसं वचः ।
अस्मिन्राजर्षिवंशे हि त्वमेकः प्राज्ञसंमतः ॥
iast:
śrotumicchāmi te dharmyaṃ paraṃ naiḥśreyasaṃ vacaḥ |
asminrājarṣivaṃśe hi tvamekaḥ prājñasaṃmataḥ ||
english: I wish to hear from you words that are righteous and lead to the highest good, for in this line of royal sages you alone are held to be wise.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
रजा लक्षणसंपन्नस्त्रैलोक्यस्याधिपो भवेत् ।
प्रेष्यस्ते प्रेषितश्चैव धृतराष्ट्र युधिष्ठिरः ॥
iast:
rajā lakṣaṇasaṃpannastrailokyasyādhipo bhavet |
preṣyaste preṣitaścaiva dhṛtarāṣṭra yudhiṣṭhiraḥ ||
english: A king endowed with every mark would be lord of the three worlds; yet Yudhishthira, your servant, was sent away by you, Dhritarashtra.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
विपरीततरश्च त्वं भागधेये न संमतः ।
अर्चिषां प्रक्षयाच्चैव धर्मात्मा धर्मकोविदः ॥
iast:
viparītataraśca tvaṃ bhāgadheye na saṃmataḥ |
arciṣāṃ prakṣayāccaiva dharmātmā dharmakovidaḥ ||
english: You are quite the opposite, not counted worthy of a share, though righteous and learned in dharma, because of the loss of your eyesight.
